answer.likely_cause: The RADIUS server now asks MFA users for a one-time code after their password, using an Access-Challenge, but this NAS can't show that second prompt, so it treats the request for a code as a rejection and the user is never asked.

evidence.line: nas-1 | 2026-11-03T21:52:12Z nas: Access-Challenge from radius:1812 for heidi discarded: challenge-response not enabled (treated as Access-Reject)
evidence.why: The NAS discards the Access-Challenge because it does not support challenge-response.

evidence.line: radius-1 | 2026-11-03T21:52:12.594231072Z Tue Nov  3 21:52:12 2026 : Auth: Challenge sent: [heidi] (from client nas port 0)
evidence.why: The RADIUS server sent an Access-Challenge to the NAS.

fix_steps: Check if the NAS supports RADIUS challenge-response and enable it if possible.
If the NAS does not support challenge-response, consider appending the code to the password for that NAS only.
answer.customer_reply: Thank you for the details. The most likely cause is that the RADIUS server is now asking for a one-time code after the password, but your NAS does not support this challenge-response feature. As a result, the login attempt is rejected without asking for the code. We recommend checking if your NAS supports RADIUS challenge-response and enabling it if possible. If it does not support it, you may need to append the code to the password for that NAS only.
